- Overestimate prices during sentiment spikes (high sentiment → forecast too high, especially in early/medium horizon).
- Underestimate late-period price surges (especially after sentiment shifts to bullish; model lags in catching momentum).
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (forecast peaks too early or too high, then drops below true).
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after strong upward runs, underestimating rebound.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently underestimate late-period price action (last 5–7 days of forecast often too low).
- Sentiment correlation: when sentiment is >0.7, model should adjust upward by 2–5% to avoid underestimating bullish momentum.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was high 3–5 days prior, model should add 1–3% to forecast to account for delayed impact.
- Avoid “flat” forecasts when sentiment is rising — model often fails to capture accelerating trend.
